items.title: OpenAI Cuts Cursor Over Trust, Not Technology
points: OpenAI will end model access for coding tool Cursor on November 12, after Cursor's parent company Anysphere was acquired by SpaceX.
OpenAI cited trust concerns tied to Elon Musk's ownership and history of contract violations by Musk-owned companies, not technical issues.
It remains unclear whether Anthropic, which powers Cursor's Claude integration, will also terminate its relationship with Cursor.
Cursor must now rely more heavily on Anthropic's Claude model and its own in-house Composer model to stay viable.

items.title: South Korea's Free AI Initiative
points: South Korea will roll out free, unlimited AI services to all citizens by late 2026, delivered through three consortia: SK Telecom, KT, and Kakao.
512 Nvidia B200 chips (high-performance AI accelerator chips used to train and run AI models) will be distributed during 2026 to power the effort.
Starting in 2027, the government will cover part of the operating costs, with companies funding the rest.

Rules require at least 50% of model compute to come from independent Korean-made foundation models (large general-purpose AI models), plus 30% from other domestic developers, to strengthen the local AI industry.

items.title: Meta's Robot Workforce Trials in Data Centers
points: Meta is testing robots from vendors Watney Robotics, Kinova, and ABB for data center tasks like cable swapping, server reboots, rack moving, and equipment inspection.
The robots currently need continuous human supervision because they struggle with tangled cables, battery life, navigation obstacles, and inspection accuracy.
One worker estimated that successful cable-swapping robots could eventually replace up to 80% of certain job functions, though Meta has not released official productivity forecasts.

items.title: Prediction Market Regulation Split Heads to Supreme Court
points: The Ninth Circuit federal appeals court (covering nine Western U.S. states) ruled that prediction markets like Kalshi can be regulated by states as gambling.

This contradicts an earlier Third Circuit ruling that favored federal financial regulation over prediction markets, creating a circuit split (when two federal appeals courts reach opposing conclusions on the same legal question).
Such splits typically prompt Supreme Court intervention to set a uniform national rule.
The ruling exposes Kalshi and similar platforms to potential state-level bans or tighter regulation in California, Arizona, and six other Ninth Circuit states.

items.title: X Uncovers China-Linked Fake Account Network
points: X identified 200,000 fake accounts tied to China, including 200 accounts specifically spreading AI-generated anti-data-center propaganda.
The propaganda falsely claimed new data centers would strain power grids and raise household electricity prices.
The fake content was generated using OpenAI's own AI tools.
